uncited: Unlike [Delta tracking](985-delta-tracking.md), which focuses on free-path sampling in heterogeneous media, the Path Integral Framework provides the rigorous mathematical measure and contribution function definition that these samplers estimate [873-path-integral-framework.md].
All methods in this family rely on the statistical estimation of the integral form of the radiative transfer equation.
The core mechanism involves generating random paths through the medium and estimating the contribution of each path to the final image.
Paths are constructed by sampling interaction points (scattering or absorption events) along rays.
For heterogeneous media, techniques like Delta Tracking sample the continuous distribution exactly without grid constraints [985-delta-tracking.md].

*   **Multiple Importance Sampling (MIS):** Combining multiple sampling strategies (e.g., light sampling vs. path sampling) to reduce variance in difficult lighting scenarios [1167-multiple-importance-sampling-for-volumetric-path-tracing.md].

*   **Biased Sampling:** Deliberately biasing the random walk to exit the medium faster (e.g., Dwivedi Sampling) to reduce the number of "lost" paths, accepting a small bias for significant variance reduction [5537-dwivedi-sampling.md].
